ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An object starts falling from rest from a sufficiently high place, and the graph of the relationship between its acceleration a and time t is measured as shown in the figure. Given the gravitational acceleration $g=10m/s^{2}$, within 0~2s, the resistance force on the object is directly proportional to what quantity?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is acceleration a, with unit m·s^-2, and the horizontal axis is time t, with unit s; the a-t graph is a straight line, linearly decreasing from a=10 m/s^2 at t=0 to a=0 at t=2 s. Therefore, within 0~2 s it can be written as a=10-5t. Reasoning: Take the downward direction as the positive direction; the object is subjected to gravity mg downward and resistance force f upward. By Newton's second law, mg-f=ma. Given g=10 m/s^2, so f=m(g-a)=m[10-(10-5t)]=5mt. The mass m is constant, therefore the resistance force f is directly proportional to the falling time t. Final answer: the falling time.
